tagline: The state's first scenic byway, slowed down on purpose.
intro: South of Ellensburg the highway leaves the wide Kittitas Valley and enters the canyon through a run of hairpin turns along its narrowest stretch. From there it follows the Yakima River's bends for about 25 miles under basalt cliffs and shrub-steppe hills, to the farms near Pomona at the Selah end of the road.

The road was finished in 1924 with tunnels blasted through the basalt, later abandoned. It was proposed as the state's first scenic corridor, in Governor Daniel J. Evans's words, for letting the traveler pass through beautiful country "at a pace enabling him to enjoy and appreciate its beauty." Once I-82 took the through traffic, the speed limit came down to discourage the trucks.
season: State of Washington Tourism says the canyon road is usually open all year and does not normally close in winter, with summer the popular time on the river.

moments.title: Umtanum Creek Recreation Area
moments.text: From the parking lot a footbridge crosses the Yakima River to a network of hiking trails, at one of five BLM recreation sites spaced along the canyon.

moments.title: Roza Dam
moments.text: The railroad crosses to the far bank here while the highway keeps uphill above a 1939 diversion dam, whose fish ladder ends in a trap where fish are counted and let go.

moments.title: Umtanum Ridge
moments.text: Near the south end the river has cut clean through Umtanum Ridge, a long fold of basalt whose Sahaptin name may mean "mouth full."

practical: Two lanes with only occasional shoulders, and cell coverage is limited through much of the canyon. Sections close each year for day-long events such as a winter cattle drive.
